([[Fayetteville, North Carolina]]) | college = [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|NC State]] (2016–2017) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | career_start = | years1 = | team1 = | highlights = *[[Atlantic Coast Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year|ACC Rookie of the Year]] (2017) *Second-team All-[[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] (2017) *ACC All-Freshman team (2017) *North Carolina [[Gatorade Player of the Year]] (2015) }} '''Dennis Smith Jr.''' (born November 25, 1997) is an American [[basketball]] player. He was ranked among the top point guards in the class of 2016 by most basketball recruiting services. He attended [[NC State University]] for one season of [[College basketball]] and earned second-team all-conference honors in the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC) as a freshman. After the season, Smith decided to forgo his remaining college eligibility and declared for the [[2017 NBA Draft]], ==High school career== Smith attended Trinity Christian School in [[Fayetteville, North Carolina]] all four years of his high school basketball career. As a Sophomore, Smith averaged 13.4 [[points per game]] and 6.1 [[Assist (basketball)|assists]] while leading the Trinity Christian Crusaders to a State Championship in 2014. In the 2013-14 High School OT holiday invitational, Smith scored a career high 42 points. As a junior, he averaged 21.8 points per game and was named the [[Gatorade Basketball Player of the Year]] for North Carolina.[http://www.fayobserver.com/sports/high_school/trinity-christian-s-dennis-smith-jr-named-n-c-gatorade/article_52654774-ac9f-5845-a296-267720d39913.html Trinity Christian's Dennis Smith Jr. named N.C. Gatorade Basketball Player of the Year] Prior to his senior year, he [[Torn ACL|tore his ACL]], causing him to miss the entire season.[http://www.foxsports.com/college-basketbal/story/dennis-smith-jr-is-110-percent-healthy-and-ready-to-lead-nc-state-to-a-big-season-080316 Dennis Smith Jr. is '110 percent' healthy, ready to lead NC State to a big season] more highlights from his junior season include scoring 35 points at the 2014-15 National Hoopfest, and recording 38 points in the 2014-15 High School OT holiday invitational against a very talented [[Orangeville Prep]] team that featured Future NBA players [[Thon Maker]] and [[Jamal Murray]]. Smith received surgery weeks later after the injury. Before the injury he sustained before his Senior season, in the summer of 2015, Smith competed on the [[Adidas]] Uprising Circuit for the AAU team, Team Loaded North Carolina (NC) alongside [[Edrice Adebayo|Bam Adebayo]]. He led his team to win the Adidas Uprising Gauntlet 17u championship. Smith averaged 16.2 points, 4.8 rebounds, and 6.9 assists in 11 games on the [[Adidas]] Uprising Gauntlet Circuit.{{Cite news|url=http://www.fayobserver.com/598bce94-26be-11e5-9c5d-3f1b028ec345.html|title=Dennis Smith, Team Loaded conclude play at Adidas Uprising Gauntlet Finale|last=Strelow|first=Bret|date=July 10, 2015|work=Www.fayobserver.com|access-date=April 25, 2017|archive-url=|archive-date=|dead-url=}} Weeks later Smith and his team played in the [[ESPNU]] summer showcase against indiana elite which he led Team Loaded to victory.{{Cite news|url=http://www.fayobserver.com/270680ae-341a-11e5-8392-7ff436d3ea8f.html|title=Dennis Smith jr, Team Loaded bounce back from semifinals lost, end Adidas Uprising event in strong fashion|last=Strelow|first=Bret|date=July 27, 2015|work=Www.fayobserver.com|access-date=April 25, 2017|archive-url=|archive-date=|dead-url=}} Smith also appeared in the [[Nike, Inc.|Nike]] Elite Youth Basketball League (EYBL) Circuit for the AAU Team Penny, sponsored by former [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] superstar [[Penny Hardaway]]. He played 9 games for Team Penny while averaging 12.0 points and 2.9 assists in the EYBL circuit. Smith participated in other events and camps such as the NBPA Top 100 camp, Steph Curry Select Camp, Adidas Nations, and the Elite 24 Invitational. Smith was rated by [[Scout.com]], [[Rivals.com]], and 247sports as a five-star recruit and ranked No. 7 by 247sports, while [[Scout.com]] ranked him the No. 4 in the Class of 2016.http://www.scout.com/player/177477-dennis-smithhttps://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/493 He committed to [[NC State University]] to play college basketball.[http://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/13626075/dennis-smith-jr-no-1-point-guard-espn-100-2016-says-attend-nc-state Dennis Smith Jr., No. 1 point guard in ESPN 100 for 2016, picks NC State][http://www.newsobserver.com/sports/high-school/article52697690.html Dennis Smith Jr. ready to enroll early at NC State] ==College career== ===North Carolina State (2016–2017)=== In December 2015, Smith graduated early from Trinity Christian School due to his injury before his senior year in high school. In January 2016, Smith enrolled at [[North Carolina State University]]. Smith had an opportunity to attend classes and rehab from his ACL and PCL tear that he suffered earlier on last year, thus getting an early start on his freshman year. Smith began his freshman season playing in two exhibition games against [[Lynn University]] and [[Barton College]].{{Cite news|url=http://www.newsobserver.com/sports/college/acc/nc-state/article113187353.html|title=Defense lifts NC State to 112-60 rout of Barton|last=Giglo|first=Joe|date=November 7, 2016|work=|access-date=January 26, 2017|via=Www.newsobserver.com}}{{Cite news|url=http://www.newsobserver.com/sports/college/acc/nc-state/article112441112.html|title=Smith leads NC State to preseason rout of lynn|last=Giglo|first=Joe|date=November 3, 2016|work=|access-date=January 26, 2017|via=Www.newsobserver.com}} In his debut for the Wolfpack, Smith played 36 minutes and dished out five assists in a 81-79 victory against [[Georgia Southern]].{{Cite news|url=http://www.newsobserver.com/sports/college/acc/nc-state/article114302978.html|title=Just the beginning for NC State, Smith in Rocky debut - decock|last=Decock|first=Luke|date=November 11, 2016|work=|access-date=January 26, 2017|via=Www.newsobserver.com}} On November 21, 2016 Smith recorded a career high 24 points to go along with 8 assist defeating [[Saint Joseph's University]] 73-63 in the [[Paradise Jam Tournament]]. On November 26, 2016 he scored a season high 30 points, 6 rebounds, and 7 assist to help NC State defeat [[Loyola University Chicago]]. On December 15, 2016, Smith recorded 22 points and 6 assists, leading NC State to defeat [[Appalachian State]]. On December 19, 2016, Smith earned ACC Freshman of the Week honors. On January 4, 2017, Smith achieved a triple-double -- 27 points, 11 rebounds, and 11 assists -- in a win against the [[Virginia Tech Hokies]], making him and [[Julius Hodge]] the only two NC State players to record this feat. On January 23, 2017 Smith scored another career high 32 points and 6 Assist in a 84-82 victory against the [[Duke Blue Devils]] leading NC State to its first win in [[Cameron Indoor Stadium]] since 1995.{{Cite news|url=http://www.newsobserver.com/sports/spt-columns-blogs/luke-decock/article128333979.html|title=Dennis Smith jr and NC State upset Jayson Tatum and Duke|last=Decock|first=Luke|date=January 23, 2017|work=WWW.newsobserver.com|access-date=June 6, 2017|archive-url=|archive-date=|dead-url=}} Smith recorded his second triple-double--13 points, 15 assists, and 11 rebounds--of the 2016 season on February 1 in a losing effort to Syracuse. He is the only player in [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] history to record two triple-doubles against league opponents in an entire collegiate career.[http://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/dennis-smith-sets-acc-triple-double-record-but-nc-state-still-loses-things-to-know/ "Dennis Smith sets ACC triple-double record -- but NC State still loses: Things to know."] CBSSports.com. N.p., 2 February 2017. Web. 16 February 2017. On February 21, 2017, Smith scored 18 points in a 71-69 win against the [[Georgia Tech Yellowjackets]]. On March 5, 2017, Smith earned ACC Rookie of the Year honors. In 32 games for NC State in 2016-17, he averaged 18.1 points, 6.2 assist, and 1.9 steals per game. At the conclusion of his freshman season, Smith announced his intention to forgo his final three years of collegiate eligibility and enter the [[2017 NBA Draft]] where he is projected as a top ten pick.{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/19023190/north-carolina-state-wolfpack-pg-dennis-smith-jr-enter-nba-draft|title=NC State freshman Dennis Smith enters NBA draft|website=espn.com|author=Staff|date=2017-03-28|accessdate=2017-03-28}} ===College statistics=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2016–17]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2016–17 NC State Wolfpack men's basketball team|NC State]] | 32 || 32 || 34.8 || .455 || .359 || .715 || 4.6 || 6.2 || 1.9 || .4 || 18.1 {{S-end}} ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== *[http://gopack.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=3935&path=mbball NC State Wolfpack bio] {{DEFAULTSORT:Smith, Dennis}} [[Category:1997 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Basketball players from North Carolina]] [[Category:NC State Wolfpack men's basketball players]] [[Category:Point guards]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Fayetteville, North Carolina]]
